WhatsApp earlier this year first introduced the Liquid Glass design on iOS, and is now extending the design to more interface elements. Here are the details you need to know.

Liquid Glass design is coming to WhatsApp's drawing editor and video player

If this topic sounds familiar, please bear with us: WhatsApp is expanding its Liquid Glass redesign to more parts of the app.

After more than six months of testing, WhatsApp finally rolled out its first wave of Liquid Glass changes more broadly earlier this year.

At that time, WhatsApp's parent company was also working to bring the new design to elements such as the voice message player, message reactions, and contextual menus, but these changes were limited to the app's beta version at the time.

According to WABetaInfo, the latest WhatsApp iOS beta shows that the company is preparing to extend the Liquid Glass visual effects to more interface elements, including the progress bars of the drawing editor and video player.

WABetaInfo reported as follows:

It's worth noting that some 9to5Mac readers have occasionally reported that their iPhones have not yet received the first wave of Liquid Glass updates; however, this news shows that Meta continues to adopt this new visual language, not only on iOS, but also extending to macOS and iPadOS.

Back to the topic, WABetaInfo pointed out: "This feature is still under development and beta users cannot try it out for now."
